summary: Robert Deliège is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford from ~1982 to 1985. He held posts at the University of Kerala and the Université catholique de Louvain, where he was professor around 1989.

Robert Duquenne is a specialist in Tantric Buddhism working in Buddhist studies and Japanology. His career includes attested appointments at Hōbōgirin in 1981 and the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2009.

Robert E. Buswell Jr. is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (~1979–1985) and studied under Kusan Sunim, Gerald James Larson, Lewis Lancaster, and others. He served as professor at UCLA (attested 1986–1994, ~1993).

Robert E. Morrell works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and teacher William H. McCullough, and held a post at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

Robert E. Svoboda works in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Oklahoma (~1970–1972) and under Vimalananda (~1975–1983), and held adjunct posts at the Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health in 2008.

Robert F. Rhodes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who was a Ph.D. candidate at Harvard University. He served as professor at Otani University (attested 1993–1997, 2012–2014) and was a committee member at the Otani Society (attested 2000).

Robert Florida is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and later as an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).
Robert Ford Campany is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He was a professor at Indiana University (~1989–2004) and was affiliated with Vanderbilt University around 2010.

Robert Gardner worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Harvard University (~1944–1958), where he later served as professor from ~1957 to 1997, and held a post at the University of Puget Sound.

Robert H. Brower was a scholar of Japanology who studied at Harvard University (~1940–1944) and the University of Michigan (~1947–1952). He served as Chairman of the Department of Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at the University of Michigan (~1966–1986).

Robert H. Sharf specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology, earning his PhD at the University of Michigan. He held posts at McMaster University, the University of Michigan, and UC Berkeley, where he was appointed D. H. Chen Distinguished Professor.

Robert J. Miller was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1956–1988) and at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Robert Kritzer is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini in 1995. He served as an associate professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).

Robert L. Brown worked in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as curator in South and Southeast Asian art at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1981–2014) and as professor at UCLA (~1984–2014).

Robert Lenz was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Tartu Governorate Gymnasium and the Imperial University of Dorpat (1825–1828). He was Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University from ~1835 to 1836.

Robert M. Gimello was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who earned his PhD at Columbia University (~1968–1976). He headed Oriental Studies and was professor emeritus at the University of Arizona, and served as professor at Harvard University (attested 2004–2007).

Robert Maclagan was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1836–1837) and Addiscombe Military Seminary (~1837–1839). He served as Principal of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

Robert Magliola is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at Princeton University (~1966–1970). He was Distinguished Chair Professor at National Taiwan University (~1990–1998) and professor at Assumption University (~1998–2003).

Robert Mayer specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a dissertation at the University of Bristol (-1985), earned a Ph.D. at Leiden University supervised by Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen, and joined Oxford's Oriental Studies Faculty in 2002.

Robert Needham Cust was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Eton College (~1834–1840) and Haileybury and Imperial Service College (~1840–1842). He served in the Bengal Civil Service from ~1843 to 1867.
